prize_parts.citation: for the theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of the quantum spin Hall effect and the topological classification of insulating electronic states

statement.case_for: I keep topological insulators at the top after reading the other ballots. The prize would honour a change in how electronic phases are classified: band topology, the Z2 invariant and protected edge states, introduced in a concrete theoretical proposal (Kane and Mele, quantum spin Hall effect in graphene) and then made unambiguous by a decisive experiment (Molenkamp's HgTe quantum wells, with quantised edge conductance). Over fifteen to twenty years the idea has been tested in many material families and with several techniques, and it has changed how the community searches for materials, including computational searches that rest on first-principles band structures. That is a broad, mature and stable result, and the recognition is overdue. The Kane, Mele, Molenkamp trio is the most compact configuration that joins prediction and experiment without leaning on the 3D or quantum anomalous Hall strands.
statement.case_against: The credit story is incomplete. The HgTe proposal by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang was what directed Molenkamp's experiment, and it falls outside the credited names. The 3D topological insulators (Fu, Kane, Mele; Hasan's ARPES work) and the quantum anomalous Hall effect (Xue) are further strands that a three-person limit forces us to leave out or fold in. A prize on the quantum spin Hall effect alone can look narrower than the field it started. The 2016 prize on topological phases of matter also means some members may see this as a close follow-up, though that prize concerned topological phase transitions and the quantum Hall plateaux rather than time-reversal-invariant band insulators. My recollection of the priority history is not independently verified.

responses.point: Kroll ranks optical lattice clocks (B022) first as an enabling instrument-level advance in frequency metrology, with a clean two-person credit and independent confirmation across many laboratories.
responses.response: I accept that the lattice-clock credit is cleaner than the topological one, and that cleanliness of attribution counts for something. But a clean attribution does not make a stronger case for the prize. I weigh B022 below topological insulators because it is a gain in precision within a field recognised in 2005 (frequency combs) and 2012 (ion control), whereas topological band theory introduced a classification principle that spread into materials, photonics and device concepts. Clocks are a strong alternative and I list B022 as one, but I would not let tidy credit decide the first place, and the redefinition of the second is a metrology milestone rather than a discovery in nature.

responses.point: Johansson ranks the topological theme first too but proposes Kane and Molenkamp only (B004 style), noting that credit is split across the theory, the HgTe experiment, 3D topological insulators and the quantum anomalous Hall effect, so any two- or three-person prize omits major contributors.
responses.response: I agree that every configuration here leaves out major contributors, and I take that seriously. Where I differ is on the third name. Mele co-authored the Z2 theory with Kane in the same two papers, so dropping him to make room for Xue's quantum anomalous Hall effect or for Hasan splits the theoretical credit and adds a later, distinct achievement. I prefer a prize that stays on the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 classification, with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp. I accept that Xue's work could be recognised separately later and I list B004 only as a fallback if the committee wants the QAH strand in.

responses.point: Lindroth puts B022 first and B004 second, calling the topological theme a natural successor to the 2016 prize and noting that credit among the theory pioneers and the experimental groups is contested.
responses.response: I agree that it is a natural successor to 2016, but I do not think that overlap counts against it. The 2016 citation covered topological phase transitions and phases in 1D and 2D with broken time-reversal symmetry, while the Z2 classification and protected edge states in time-reversal-invariant insulators are a separate conceptual step. On the contested credit, I would hold the committee to the narrowest defensible discovery, the quantum spin Hall effect, rather than let the dispute push us toward a different candidate. Contested priority is a reason to define the citation carefully, not to defer.

responses.point: Pearce ranks B022 first, B002 (baryon acoustic oscillations) second and the Kane, Mele, Molenkamp trio third, noting that the omitted HgTe theorists, the 2D versus 3D strands and Hasan's exclusion could all be contested.
responses.response: We broadly agree on the trio and on the attribution difficulties, which makes me comfortable that this is the right configuration if the committee turns to topological insulators. I would put it higher than third. The BAO case is a transparent observational triumph, but its credit sits with large survey collaborations and with theory outside the credited names, which is a harder attribution problem than ours. I accept your point that Hasan's exclusion can be challenged, and I would rather state it openly in the citation than fold the 3D strand in.

responses.point: Danielsson ranks magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (B030) first as a rare prediction-then-discovery pair that created a very large new field, and notes the superconducting pairing mechanism remains debated.
responses.response: I rank B030 second and I share the admiration for the clean theory and experiment pair. My reservation is timing. Eight years after the experiment the origin of the correlated states and of the superconductivity is not settled, and the results are sensitive to twist-angle disorder, which I know from the standpoint of calculations is hard to treat. The topological case has a stable interpretation that has survived two decades of materials work. I do not think B030 should be rejected, and it is my first alternative, but I would let the field settle a few more years.

uncertainties: Whether the citation should cover only the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 classification, or also 3D topological insulators and the ARPES work, which would change who belongs.
How much weight to give the HgTe proposal by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, which sits outside the credited names, one of whom is deceased.
Whether the committee regards the 2016 prize as having absorbed enough of this territory to argue for waiting.
My account of priority and attribution details rests on my own background knowledge and was not independently verified from the supplied files.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for the shortlisted ballots. My field of electronic-structure theory and first-principles materials calculations is adjacent to the topological-materials theme, and my Uppsala materials theory group works on related methods, but my profile documents no personal or institutional tie to Kane, Mele, Molenkamp or the other credited candidates, so I do not think recusal is required.
